Testing release: Windows and Linux installed-update qualification is not complete. This release does not claim platform qualification. Windows Authenticode is deferred.

Versión de prueba: la cualificación de actualización instalada en Windows y Linux no está completa. Esta versión no declara cualificación de plataforma. Authenticode de Windows está aplazado.

GitOdile 0.3.0

Highlights

- Overview walks you through Changes, Save and Publish and points out the next step, and Changes and History are now the two tabs of one Work screen.
- Lines shows where each version line left the main line, what it changes and whether its work is already there, even as copies.
- The new Console runs Git commands you type, read-only unless you choose an advanced mode where every change is shown first.
- GitOdile has a new mascot and icon, and Settings offers colour themes: Catppuccin, Nord, Tokyo Night, Dracula, Solarized and Gruvbox beside its own light and dark.
- Updates follow one channel, so everyone gets every release, and the update dialog lists what a new version brings, in your language.

GitOdile 0.3.0 reorganises the everyday workflow around three steps, rebuilds the version lines screen, adds a Git console and gives GitOdile a new look. It is also the first release on a single update channel: there are no separate stable and preview builds any more, and every installation is offered every release.

- Overview is rebuilt as one page: a band of three steps, Changes, Save and Publish, highlights the next thing to do, and Recent history marks the saved versions that are not published yet, with publishing one click away.
- Changes and History are now the two tabs of a single Work screen, sharing one layout, one diff toolbar and one find. Saving happens from one box under the file list, which states the plan before you save, and both file lists can be read as folders.
- When there is nothing to save, the Changes tab explains where the project stands (unpublished versions, newer changes on the remote, no saved versions yet, or an old version checked out) and offers the one action that fits.
- History shows each saved version as a single view: its message and details fold away, and the changes are always visible. Rows mark your own versions, tags and the ones not published yet, and a filter shows only tagged versions.
- Lines is rebuilt around the same shape. The selected line shows where it left the main line, the versions each side saved since, what it changes, and whether its work already reached the main line, including as squashed or rebased copies. Lines are created and renamed in place, with their names checked before you press. Deleting a line whose work is only on the main line as copies keeps a recovery point for its original versions first.
- A new Console screen runs the Git commands you type, such as git log --graph -- src/ or git blame file, reading each line itself without a shell. It is read-only by default: help git lists what it accepts, and anything that would change the project, reach the remote, run another program or leave the project is refused with the reason. Twenty short names, such as look, today or unpublished, run common queries, and you can add your own.
- Settings → Console offers two more console modes behind a confirmation. Advanced also runs commands such as git add, git commit -m, git switch, git stash push, git fetch, a fast-forward git pull and git push, each printed first with what it will change and run only when you answer yes; root runs them without the question. Neither runs a command if the project changed in between, and commands that rewrite history or can discard work stay unavailable.
- The Projects screen stays reachable from More actions and the command palette while projects are open, to open another one, and the keyboard-shortcuts sheet groups every shortcut and draws the keys as your platform names them.
- Save and Publish open at once in their final shape and confirm their plan while you read it, and first loads draw the layout they are about to fill.
- Every action dialog shares one layout, and finished results such as a publish or getting project changes close with a short notice instead of another dialog.
- The status bar shows how many lines changed in your working files, and its cloud opens publishing while there is something to send.
- Notifications are an inbox: an unread dot replaces the red counter, and entries can be dismissed one by one.
- Settings offers colour themes: GitOdile's own light and dark, plus Catppuccin (Mocha, Latte and Frappé), Nord, Tokyo Night, Dracula, Solarized (Dark and Light) and Gruvbox (Dark and Light). Every theme keeps text, buttons, the diff and its syntax colours readable, measured against the WCAG AA contrast floors.
- Updates follow one channel. Settings → Updates no longer asks you to choose between stable and preview: every installation, including the 0.2.0-preview builds, is offered each new release.
- The update feed now carries each release's highlights in English and Spanish. Builds from this one on show them in the update dialog, in your language, when a newer version is offered; 0.2.0-preview.12 still shows the plain notes when it offers this update.
- The version is shown on its own, without a channel label. About leads with the app's identity and says whether the build is up to date.
- GitOdile has a new mascot, a crocodile in sunglasses whose crest is a commit graph. Its icon is the same amber tile on every platform and at every size, and the mascot greets you on the welcome, About and Console screens. The Windows installer carries the icon and artwork, is available in English and Spanish, and keeps desktop and Start-menu shortcut icons intact across updates.
- Windows is provided as an NSIS installer. Authenticode remains deliberately deferred, so Windows may show an unknown-publisher or SmartScreen warning.
- Linux is provided as an AppImage.
- Both packages verify updates with the production Tauri updater key and the public latest.json feed in martinezelx/gitodile; preview.json carries the same release for installed 0.2.0-preview builds.
- macOS remains disabled and no macOS package is included.

Publishing this release does not declare either target qualified.

highlights.en: Overview walks you through Changes, Save and Publish and points out the next step, and Changes and History are now the two tabs of one Work screen.
highlights.es: Resumen te guía por Cambios, Guardar y Publicar y te señala el siguiente paso, y Cambios e Historial son ahora las dos pestañas de una sola pantalla, Trabajo.

highlights.en: Lines shows where each version line left the main line, what it changes and whether its work is already there, even as copies.
highlights.es: Líneas muestra dónde se separó cada línea de versiones de la principal, qué cambia y si su trabajo ya está en ella, aunque sea como copias.

highlights.en: The new Console runs Git commands you type, read-only unless you choose an advanced mode where every change is shown first.
highlights.es: La nueva Consola ejecuta los comandos Git que escribes, en solo lectura salvo que elijas un modo avanzado que muestra cada cambio antes.

highlights.en: GitOdile has a new mascot and icon, and Settings offers colour themes: Catppuccin, Nord, Tokyo Night, Dracula, Solarized and Gruvbox beside its own light and dark.
highlights.es: GitOdile estrena mascota e icono, y Ajustes ofrece temas de color: Catppuccin, Nord, Tokyo Night, Dracula, Solarized y Gruvbox, además de su claro y su oscuro.

highlights.en: Updates follow one channel, so everyone gets every release, and the update dialog lists what a new version brings, in your language.
highlights.es: Las actualizaciones siguen un único canal, así que todo el mundo recibe cada versión, y el diálogo de actualización muestra qué trae, en tu idioma.
